title: Efficiency and AI systems
body: Efficiency and AI systems Why does changing batch size speed up a model? Why can a program struggle before GPU memory is full? Why can throughput improve while users wait longer? These questions arise when models meet software and hardware. Different implementations of the same model can run at very different speeds. Data movement, operator implementations, memory allocation, request scheduling, and communication between devices all affect hardware utilization. Model size, context length, and precision also connect systems questions to model design. Research themes Training memory and communication: parameters, gradients, optimizer states, and multi-GPU parallelism. Kernels and hardware: computation, memory access, numerical precision, and execution scheduling. Inference serving: latency, throughput, caching, concurrency, and cost. How models use less compute and memory 01 Weight quantization 02 KV cache 03 Continuous batching 04 Pipeline parallelism Research milestones 2020 Distributed training 2022 Attention kernel 2023 Quantization 2023 vLLM · serving cache 2020 ZeRO: partition redundant training state Follow what each sharding stage distributes and what communication it introduces. Memory savings and throughput are separate measurements. Distributed training ↗ 2022 FlashAttention: change data movement Identify which intermediate tensors are avoided and how tiling reduces memory transfers while retaining exact attention. Attention kernel ↗ 2023 SmoothQuant: make low precision practical Follow how activation outliers are handled and which kernels execute INT8 operations. Assess quality and speed on the hardware used in the study. Quantization ↗ 2023 PagedAttention: manage a growing KV cache Trace logical token positions to cache blocks. Inspect fragmentation, sharing, concurrency, and serving latency together. vLLM · serving cache ↗ Key concepts Throughput and latency Throughput measures work completed per unit time; latency measures how long a request takes. Larger batches can improve throughput while increasing queueing time. Prefill / decode Prefill processes the input context; decode generates output step by step. Their compute and memory-access patterns differ, so a single speed measurement is insufficient. KV cache Stored attention keys and values for processed tokens avoid repeated computation during generation. Context length and concurrent requests consume cache memory. Quantization Lower-precision representations reduce storage and some computation costs. Speedups depend on hardware and kernel support. Connect an optimization to its bottleneck Start with tensor shapes, matrix multiplication, numerical precision, and the difference between memory capacity and memory bandwidth. Research engineering introduces profiling and measurement. Then follow one training step or one generation request from data movement to computation and output. Technique Main resource problem A common misconception FlashAttention Data transfers between GPU memory levels and storage of intermediate attention results It reorganizes exact attention; it does not make dense attention linear in sequence length. Quantization Numerical storage and supported low-precision computation Fewer bits do not guarantee faster execution on every device or workload. ZeRO Replicated parameter, gradient, and optimizer state in distributed training Sharding saves memory while adding communication and scheduling constraints. PagedAttention Allocation and sharing of a growing KV cache during serving Cache management is distinct from reducing the network's parameter count. The FlashAttention paper is a useful example of changing data movement while preserving the mathematical operation. End-to-end gains depend on how much time the optimized component originally consumed; speeding up a small component cannot remove the rest of the workload. Compute, memory access, and execution overhead GPUs can compute quickly, but an operation also requires moving data through memory and launching and scheduling kernels. Compute-bound, memory-bound, and overhead-bound workloads require different optimizations. Horace He's Making Deep Learning go Brrrr explains these bottlenecks. FlashAttention uses tiling to reduce reads and writes to GPU memory. Quantization lowers the storage and computational requirements of numerical representations, while operator fusion can reduce intermediate results and scheduling overhead. Actual gains depend on tensor shapes, precision, and hardware implementation. The PyTorch Performance Tuning Guide covers common optimization approaches. Latency, throughput, memory, and quality Interactive services may prioritize time to first token and tail latency; offline batches may prioritize throughput. Memory and cost also constrain deployment. Larger batches can improve hardware utilization while increasing an individual request's waiting time. Longer contexts increase computation and cache requirements, while lower precision can affect model quality. A systems study therefore needs to describe both its workload and optimization goal. Comparisons under the same hardware and request conditions help establish where a design saves time or memory. Distributed training and inference Large-model training distributes parameters, gradients, optimizer states, and computation. Communication between devices introduces synchronization and waiting. Inference services must also manage KV caches, batching, and request scheduling. Methods such as ZeRO and PagedAttention address different parts of these storage and execution problems. How To Scale Your Model connects model computation, memory, communication, and parallelism. Machine Learning Systems covers the components and design of ML systems. MIT 6.5940, 2024 develops model compression, quantization, and efficient computation. Case studies and research resources Purshow's systems and architecture notes analyze concrete designs. More courses and projects appear in the systems catalog , with related work from teams such as MIT HAN Lab . AI tools can also assist with reading code and writing performance-analysis scripts. Design a testable AI-systems study Question and controls: identify training, inference, storage, or serving objectives. Specify quality targets or thresholds. Apart from the system variable under study, match hardware, numerical precision, input/output lengths, and concurrency. Distinguish algorithmic compute reduction from execution efficiency. Evaluation: record warm-up, caching, batch size, peak memory, throughput, latency distributions, and failure rates. To estimate latency percentiles, use enough requests and define the measurement window. Distributed studies should report device count, communication, and scaling efficiency. Limits: lower precision or shorter outputs can affect quality and latency. Reporting only the fastest run is insufficient. Follow the version, scenario, and quality constraints of any official benchmark used. Research design · Data and evaluation Research engineering connects environment records, profiling, benchmarking, DDP, and minimal services. Check correctness and identify bottlenecks before trying to speed up a system. When evaluating a service, examine failures, queues, timeouts, and recovery as well as kernel speed. Representative papers 01 2020 · Distributed training ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models How much memory is wasted by replicating training state on every GPU? Read paper summary ↗ 2020 · SC 2020 × ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models Original paper ↗ Project and code ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Rajbhandari et al. (2020), Fig. 1 · Original paper Research question How much memory is wasted by replicating training state on every GPU? Core method Progressively partition optimizer states, gradients, and parameters, communicating required pieces when needed. Why this paper It explains why training memory requirements extend beyond the parameters themselves. What to focus on Identify what each of the three stages partitions, then compare memory and communication costs. Limitations and open questions Sharding changes communication. Benefits depend on bandwidth and device count. 02 2022 · Attention kernel FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness Can attention be limited by data movement rather than multiplication count? Read paper summary ↗ 2022 · NeurIPS 2022 × FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness Original paper ↗ Project and code ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Dao et al. · Fig. 1 · Original paper Research question Can attention be limited by data movement rather than multiplication count? Core method Tile work into fast on-chip memory instead of repeatedly materializing the full attention matrix in device memory. Why this paper It shows how the same mathematical operation can have very different execution costs. What to focus on Start with GPU memory levels and tiling, then examine the I/O analysis and runtime results. Limitations and open questions Exact dense attention still has quadratic arithmetic complexity. Speedup depends on shapes, hardware, and implementation. 03 2023 · Quantization SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models Why do a few very large activations make INT8 quantization difficult? Read paper summary ↗ 2023 · ICML 2023 × SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models Original paper ↗ Project and code ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Xiao et al. (2023), Fig. 2 · Original paper Research question Why do a few very large activations make INT8 quantization difficult? Core method Redistribute scale between weights and activations with an equivalent transformation, then quantize. Why this paper It connects outliers, numerical error, and hardware execution in one example. What to focus on Start with activation outliers and scale migration, then accuracy and speed comparisons. Limitations and open questions The pre-quantization transformation is equivalent; quantization still introduces error. Representative calibration data and suitable INT8 kernels matter. 04 2023 · vLLM · serving cache Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention How can a serving system avoid wasting KV-cache memory when request lengths vary? Read paper summary ↗ 2023 · SOSP 2023 × Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention Original paper ↗ Project and code ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Kwon et al. (2023), Fig. 6 · Original paper Research question How can a serving system avoid wasting KV-cache memory when request lengths vary? Core method Split the cache into blocks, map logical sequences to noncontiguous storage, and support cache sharing. Why this paper It connects operating-system paging to the capacity of a model-serving system. What to focus on Start with fragmentation and block mapping, then throughput under matched latency conditions. Limitations and open questions It optimizes cache management. Concurrency gains must be assessed with latency targets and request lengths.

title: Interdisciplinary AI: starting with questions from other fields
body: Interdisciplinary AI: starting with questions from other fields AI contributes to molecular screening, protein design, weather forecasting, medical imaging, and mathematical proof. These fields ask different questions: predicting a property, proposing a design, approximating an equation solver, or verifying a construction. The domain determines what the data mean and what evidence is needed to support a conclusion. Choose one domain and one kind of question You do not need to learn every field below. Start with one familiar domain and learn its units, measurement processes, and established methods alongside machine-learning foundations . Follow a single paper from its scientific question to its input representation, prediction target, and validation. Use the animations to understand the workflow; they illustrate concepts rather than reproduce a paper's results. Distinguish prediction of a measured outcome, design of a candidate, simulation of a system, and decision-making about the next action or measurement. A stronger predictor may help one of these steps without validating the full scientific workflow. The sections below offer suggested reading, not an exhaustive history or a ranking of models. Natural sciences and medicine Molecules, reactions, and materials Physical simulation and weather Proteins and enzymes Genomics and regulation Single cells and virtual cells EEG and neural decoding Medical imaging Mathematics, finance, and data Mathematics and algorithm discovery Finance and quantitative research Graph learning and time series Automating the research process AutoML Automated research RSI and self-improvement How AI contributes to research Pause Molecules, reactions, and materials Physical simulation and weather Proteins and enzymes Genomics and regulation Single cells and virtual cells EEG and neural decoding Medical imaging Mathematics and algorithm discovery Finance and quantitative research Graph learning and time series AutoML Automated research RSI and self-improvement Read about this field ↓ Chemistry and materials: predicting properties, planning reactions, and discovering materials Will a molecule dissolve readily in water? Is a crystal stable? What will a set of reactants produce? AI can predict properties and screen candidates from structures and experimental records. It can also learn energies and forces to reduce the computational cost of molecular dynamics. Watch the process ↗ Property prediction Represent a molecule as a graph of atoms and bonds, or as a structure with three-dimensional coordinates, to predict quantities such as solubility and energy. The MPNN paper is a classic introduction to graph learning for quantum chemistry. Reactions and synthesis Forward prediction infers products from reactants; retrosynthesis works backward from a target molecule to find precursors and synthesis routes. Molecular Transformer models the SMILES strings of reactants and products as sequences. Materials discovery and simulation GNoME combines graph networks with first-principles calculations to screen for stable crystals. Deep Potential learns potential energy to provide the energies and forces needed for molecular dynamics. Active learning uses existing results to select the next calculations or experiments. 2017 MPNN Structure → properties 2018–2019 Deep Potential / Molecular Transformer Simulation and reaction prediction 2023 GNoME Model screening + DFT validation 01 2017 · MPNN · Molecular graphs Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry How can atoms and their relationships predict molecular properties? Read paper summary ↗ 2017 · ICML × Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry Original paper ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Gilmer et al. · Fig. 1 · Original paper Research question How can atoms and their relationships predict molecular properties? Core method Update node representations through messages, then aggregate them for a molecular prediction. Why this paper It grounds graph learning in a concrete chemistry task. What to focus on Start with message passing, readout, targets, and data. Limitations and open questions The benchmark concerns quantum-chemical properties of small molecules; it does not establish transfer to larger molecules, different chemical spaces, or drug efficacy. 02 2018 · Deep Potential · Faster simulation Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics: A Scalable Model with the Accuracy of Quantum Mechanics How can accurate energy and force calculations become cheaper? Read paper summary ↗ 2018 · Physical Review Letters × Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics: A Scalable Model with the Accuracy of Quantum Mechanics Original paper ↗ Project and code ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Zhang et al., Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics, Figure 1 · Original paper Research question How can accurate energy and force calculations become cheaper? Core method Learn local atomic contributions from first-principles data while preserving problem symmetries. Why this paper An example of replacing an expensive step in a scientific computation. What to focus on Trace energies and forces into simulation, then inspect physical comparisons. Limitations and open questions Accuracy depends on the configurations covered by the data and reference calculations; new conditions need testing. Papers and learning resources Molecular Transformer ↗ 2019 · Reaction prediction GNoME ↗ 2023 · Crystal stability and materials discovery DeepChem ↗ Molecular tasks and tutorials Therapeutics Data Commons ↗ Drug discovery tasks and data DeePMD-kit ↗ Learning potential energies for molecular dynamics SMILES A string representation of molecular structure. DFT Density functional theory: a family of methods for calculating electronic structure, energy, and other properties. Physics and weather: learning solutions and predicting how systems evolve Fluid flow, heat transfer, and weather forecasting involve physical quantities that vary across space and time. AI can approximate solutions to the equations that describe these processes, or use observations to predict how physical systems evolve. Watch the process ↗ Bringing equations into training Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) incorporate equation residuals, boundary conditions, and observation errors into training. Research examines how these constraints help, and how models handle complex domains and changes across multiple scales. Learning solutions for a family of problems Neural operators learn mappings from functions to functions, such as predicting an entire flow field from initial conditions. FNO constructs operations in the frequency domain, trains on solutions to a set of problems, and then handles new input conditions. Forecasting weather and uncertainty GraphCast uses graph networks to predict global weather fields. Later probabilistic forecasting approaches describe uncertainty through multiple possible futures. Researchers compare forecast errors, performance on extreme weather, and computation time. 2019 PINNs Equation constraints in training 2021 FNO Learning mappings between functions 2023 GraphCast Predicting global weather fields 01 2021 · FNO · Neural operators Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations How can a model learn the map from input functions, such as initial conditions or coefficients, to equation solutions? Read paper summary ↗ 2021 · ICLR × Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations Original paper ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Figure 1 · Original paper Research question How can a model learn the map from input functions, such as initial conditions or coefficients, to equation solutions? Core method Parameterize integral kernels in the frequency domain to learn mappings from functions to functions for a family of partial differential equation problems. Why this paper It distinguishes solving one equation instance from learning an input-to-solution map across a family. What to focus on Start with the operator layer and the inputs and outputs, then compare errors across resolutions and equation settings. Limitations and open questions It learns a family of equations and conditions represented in the data. Resolution transfer does not guarantee boundary conditions, conservation laws, or accuracy on arbitrary new equations. Papers and learning resources PINNs ↗ The authors' introduction and examples Fourier Neural Operator ↗ 2021 · ICLR GraphCast ↗ 2023 · Science NeuralOperator ↗ Neural operator implementations and tutorials PDE A partial differential equation describes how a quantity changes with variables such as space and time. Neural operator A model that learns a mapping from an input function to an output function, such as an initial field to a future flow field. Proteins and enzymes: from sequence and structure to functional design Proteins consist of amino acid sequences, and their folded structures are closely linked to what they can do. AI can predict structures, find natural sequences with desired properties, or propose new designs. Watch the process ↗ Representation and structure prediction Protein language models learn transferable features from sequences. AlphaFold2 combines sequences, evolutionary information, and geometric relationships to predict three-dimensional structures. AlphaFold3 extends this to complexes containing proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules, and other components. Sequence and backbone design ProteinMPNN designs sequences for a given backbone; RFdiffusion generates backbones that satisfy constraints; ESM3 jointly uses sequence, structure, and function information. The design workflow then checks expression, stability, binding, or catalytic activity. Enzyme mining and engineering Enzyme mining finds candidates in natural sequence libraries; enzyme engineering modifies existing enzymes; de novo design builds new candidates around a target reaction. VenusMine retrieves candidates using structural and sequence clues, while VenusRXN matches enzymes starting from chemical reactions. 2021 AlphaFold2 Structure prediction 2022–2023 ProteinMPNN / RFdiffusion Sequence and backbone design 2025–2026 AMix-1 / AMix-2 Conditional generation and protein–text modeling Read further The experimental loop in enzyme engineering Zero-shot scoring can first rank mutations. A small amount of measured data can be used to fit a model of a specific property, while active learning uses existing results and uncertainty to choose the next experiments. Each round adds newly measured activity or stability to the data and updates the candidate ranking. Constraints in de novo design One approach finds a backbone to support a catalytic core; another organizes local interactions within an existing backbone. Catalytic geometry, foldability, stability, and reaction conditions all determine which experiments are needed next. New approaches to foundation models AMix-1 models proteins with Bayesian flow networks and explores conditioning on multiple sequence alignments and inference-time search. AMix-2 unifies protein and text modeling, using causal generation between blocks and diffusion within each block. When reading, trace the roles of conditioning inputs, candidate generation, and verifiers separately. 01 2021 · AlphaFold2 · Protein structure Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold How can sequence information support three-dimensional structure prediction? Read paper summary ↗ 2021 · Nature × Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold Original paper ↗ Project and code ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Jumper et al., AlphaFold, Figure 1(e) · CC BY 4.0 · Original paper Research question How can sequence information support three-dimensional structure prediction? Core method Combine evolutionary sequence information and residue relationships, iteratively refining representations and structure. Why this paper It connects data, geometry, and system design around a scientific problem. What to focus on Start with the architecture, CASP14 evaluation, and confidence estimates. Limitations and open questions Predicted structures and confidence estimates do not directly measure function, dynamics, or binding. Biological conclusions require evidence appropriate to those questions. 02 2025 · AMix-1 · Protein generation AMix-1: A Pathway to Test-Time Scalable Protein Foundation Model How can family information and verification feedback support protein design? Read paper summary ↗ 2025 · arXiv × AMix-1: A Pathway to Test-Time Scalable Protein Foundation Model Original paper ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Figure 1 · Original paper Research question How can family information and verification feedback support protein design? Core method Model proteins with Bayesian flow networks, use MSA context, and explore design workflows with larger inference-time search budgets. Why this paper It connects protein representations, generation, computational screening, and experimental validation. What to focus on Trace conditioning inputs, verifiers, and experimental measurements separately, comparing their roles in the iterative process. Limitations and open questions Computational verifier scores and measured activity provide different evidence. Improvements in selected protein families do not establish transfer to all proteins, functions, or conditions of use. Papers and learning resources AlphaFold3 ↗ Complex structure prediction ProteinMPNN ↗ Sequence design for a given backbone RFdiffusion ↗ Generating protein backbones ESM3 ↗ Sequence, structure, and function generation VenusMine ↗ Structure-guided enzyme mining VenusRXN ↗ Reaction-conditioned enzyme retrieval AMix-1 ↗ Bayesian flow networks and inference-time search AMix-2 ↗ Unified protein and text modeling MSA Multiple sequence alignment aligns related protein sequences to reveal evolutionary conservation and variation. Inverse folding Finding an amino acid sequence that can adopt a given protein backbone structure. Genomics: how sequence changes affect gene regulation DNA variants can alter protein coding, but they can also affect regulatory elements, expression, or splicing. Genomic models learn relationships within long sequences to predict these signals, helping researchers investigate the possible effects of a variant. Watch the process ↗ From sequence to signals Models take a DNA sequence as input and predict experimental signals, such as expression, chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding, or splicing. Comparing sequences before and after a variant Input the original and variant sequences separately and compare their predictions. AlphaGenome is a representative model combining long sequences with multiple prediction tasks. Connecting to cellular context The same variant can have different effects in different tissues or cell states. Connecting sequence models with cell models requires aligning tissues, conditions, and what is measured. Sequence modeling DNA context Understanding coding and regulatory regions Multitask prediction AlphaGenome Predicting multiple molecular signals together Variant analysis Controls and interventions Comparing predicted and experimental changes Papers and learning resources AlphaGenome research introduction ↗ Questions, inputs, outputs, and examples AlphaGenome ↗ Official tools and examples Noncoding region A region of DNA that does not directly encode a protein; some of these regions help regulate genes. Splicing The RNA processing step that joins exons and removes introns. Different splicing patterns can produce different transcripts. Cells: understanding states and predicting responses to interventions Single-cell RNA sequencing measures noisy samples of gene expression from individual cells. Researchers study not only a cell's type and state, but also how it will respond to a genetic change or a drug. Spatial omics also preserves the locations of cells within tissue. Watch the process ↗ Cell representations Geneformer, scGPT, and UCE learn gene or cell representations from large amounts of single-cell data for tasks such as annotation and integration. Data processing needs to preserve biological differences while handling sequencing depth, noise, and batch effects. Perturbations and virtual cells Given a cellular context and a genetic or drug perturbation, predict changes in expression. Virtual cells aim to connect modalities, scales, and dynamic processes more broadly; perturbation response is one clearly defined research task within this goal. Spatial relationships and biomanufacturing FLAG predicts spatial gene expression from pathology images, focusing on relationships between genes and between tissue locations. Biomanufacturing also studies metabolic networks, expression burden, and resource allocation to help propose strain modifications. Representation Geneformer / scGPT / UCE Learning cell and gene representations Relationships scPRINT / FLAG Gene networks and spatial structure Response Virtual cells Predicting states after intervention Read further States, dynamics, and dataset construction Many single-cell datasets are snapshots measured from different cells. Studying changes over time requires sampling times, lineage information, or perturbation experiments. Data should record tissue, donor, batch, and measurement modality; perturbation data should also record the target, dose, time, and control. Evaluating gene networks and spatial structure Gene association networks can be compared with known regulation and intervention data. Spatial expression prediction should compare errors at individual locations, relationships between genes, and spatial distributions. Depending on the intended use, hold out new donors, new tissues, or unseen perturbations. 01 2026 · FLAG · Spatial gene expression FLAG: Foundation model representation with Latent diffusion Alignment via Graph for spatial gene expression prediction How can tissue images predict spatial gene expression while preserving structural relationships? Read paper summary ↗ 2026 · ICML × FLAG: Foundation model representation with Latent diffusion Alignment via Graph for spatial gene expression prediction Original paper ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Figure 1 · Original paper Research question How can tissue images predict spatial gene expression while preserving structural relationships? Core method Combine spatial graph encoding with gene foundation model representations, and use a diffusion process to model expression distributions. Why this paper It shows why biological structure can matter alongside average prediction error. What to focus on Start with input images, spatial adjacency, and expression outputs, then compare errors at individual locations with structural evaluations. Limitations and open questions The outputs are expression distributions inferred from tissue images, not direct gene-expression measurements. Transfer to new patients, tissues, or platforms needs independent evaluation. Papers and learning resources Geneformer ↗ 2023 · Single-cell pretraining scGPT ↗ 2024 · Single-cell foundation model UCE ↗ Cell representations across datasets scPRINT ↗ Gene network inference FLAG ↗ 2026 · Spatial expression prediction Scanpy tutorials ↗ Single-cell processing, dimensionality reduction, and clustering Batch effect Systematic variation in data caused by differences in experimental timing, equipment, or procedures. Perturbation prediction Predicting how a cell responds to an intervention, such as gene editing or a drug, given its cellular context. EEG: from neural signals to state recognition and decoding Electroencephalography (EEG) records how electrical signals at scalp electrodes change over time. AI can help recognize states, detect events, learn representations across participants, and connect signals with stimuli such as images that participants see. Watch the process ↗ Temporal and spatial representations Electrode locations, sampling rate, filtering, and artifact handling together define the input. Models use frequency bands, changes over time, and relationships between channels. Foundation models and transfer After pretraining, the encoder can be frozen for linear probing or fine-tuned. Testing within the same participant and on new participants answers different questions. EEG-FM-Compass organizes these types of evaluation. Visual decoding and generation DreamDiffusion connects EEG representations to a pretrained image generation model and uses CLIP visual supervision. EEG-CLIP offers another alignment approach; compare how the two connect signals with images. Signal processing Time–frequency features Understanding data through channels and time 2023 DreamDiffusion Signal alignment and conditional generation 2026 EEG-FM-Compass Foundation models and transfer evaluation Read further Checking which information decoding uses First fix the stimulus and participant splits, then compare correctly paired data, shuffled pairs, and results with EEG conditioning removed. These comparisons help reveal how much the generated results depend on the input signals, and what changes with new participants, sessions, or devices. 01 2023 · DreamDiffusion · EEG decoding DreamDiffusion: Generating High-Quality Images from Brain EEG Signals How can EEG representations connect to an image generation model? Read paper summary ↗ 2023 · arXiv × DreamDiffusion: Generating High-Quality Images from Brain EEG Signals Original paper ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Figure 1 · Original paper Research question How can EEG representations connect to an image generation model? Core method Learn EEG representations through temporally masked signal modeling, combine them with CLIP visual supervision, and use the signals for conditional generation. Why this paper It helps distinguish information supplied by the signal from image priors supplied by the pretrained generator. What to focus on Trace the role of each data source and supervision signal through the training stages, then examine participant splits and controls. Limitations and open questions The study uses paired EEG and images under controlled conditions. A plausible generated image does not establish accurate decoding of arbitrary thoughts or dreams. Papers and learning resources EEG-FM-Compass ↗ 2026 · Survey and evaluation DreamDiffusion ↗ EEG-guided image generation EEG-CLIP ↗ Aligning EEG and visual representations MNE tutorials ↗ EEG data, preprocessing, and visualization Participant A person who takes part in an experiment and provides neural signals. Artifact An unwanted signal introduced by sources such as eye movements, muscle activity, or equipment. Medical imaging: locating structures and measuring motion and function In CT, MRI, or pathology images, models can delineate organs and lesions, align different images, and calculate measurements such as volume from contours and motion. Imaging methods draw on computer vision, while their research questions come from specific clinical examination and measurement needs. Watch the process ↗ Three-dimensional segmentation 3D U-Net and V-Net process volumetric data; UNet++ changes how features at multiple scales are fused; Swin UNETR introduces Transformers for context modeling. Compare how they preserve detail and use spatial relationships. Registration and functional measurement Registration estimates correspondences between images or different time frames. CMRINet jointly analyzes registration and segmentation in cardiac cine MRI, linking the identification of structures to the measurement of cardiac function. Longitudinal changes Follow-up images help researchers study how disease changes over time. Record conditions such as sampling times, treatments, and missing follow-ups. Why this paper It connects segmentation, motion estimation, and downstream functional measures without treating them as one score. What to focus on Start with the temporal dimension of cine MRI, then examine how the two tasks work together and how functional measures are calculated. Mathematics and algorithms: finding proofs and better constructions AI in mathematics can propose proof steps, add geometric constructions, or search for objects that satisfy constraints and for more efficient algorithms. A key advantage is that many candidates can be checked using formal proof systems, programs, or exact computation. Watch the process ↗ Proof search AlphaGeometry combines auxiliary constructions proposed by a language model with symbolic reasoning. Formal proof approaches express propositions and steps in systems such as Lean, where a kernel checks the proof. Mathematical constructions FunSearch lets a language model propose programs, then runs an evaluation function to select useful candidates. The paper studies combinatorial problems including cap sets. The model searches for programs that produce constructions. Algorithm discovery AlphaEvolve combines code generation, evaluators, and evolutionary search to find better algorithms and mathematical constructions. Runtime, correctness, or objective values can provide feedback. 2023 FunSearch Program generation + evaluation 2024 AlphaGeometry / AlphaProof Construction search and proofs 2025 AlphaEvolve Iterative algorithm optimization 01 2024 · AlphaGeometry · Geometry proofs Solving olympiad geometry without human demonstrations How can auxiliary constructions and symbolic reasoning work together to find a proof? Read paper summary ↗ 2024 · Nature × Solving olympiad geometry without human demonstrations Original paper ↗ Project and code ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Google DeepMind · official AlphaGeometry methodology diagram · Original paper Research question How can auxiliary constructions and symbolic reasoning work together to find a proof? Core method A symbolic engine first derives consequences from the given conditions. When needed, a language model proposes auxiliary constructions, and proof search continues. Why this paper It shows how learned proposals can work with inspectable symbolic deductions. What to focus on Trace the added constructions and the deductions they enable in a simple geometry problem, then examine how the training data are synthesized. Limitations and open questions The system uses a specified geometry representation, rule set, and construction space. Results on olympiad geometry do not establish general mathematical theorem proving. Evaluator A program that executes a candidate and returns its correctness or objective score. Finance: from text and time-series data to predictions and decisions Financial AI includes understanding financial reports and news, identifying risks, forecasting time series, constructing portfolios, and executing trades. Model inputs include structured data such as prices and trading volume, as well as text from announcements and reports. Watch the process ↗ Financial text FinGPT offers an entry point to financial language models, data, and fine-tuning. Tasks such as sentiment analysis, event extraction, and information extraction illustrate how language models can be used in this domain. Quantitative prediction and backtesting Qlib connects data processing, features, models, portfolios, and backtesting. A factor is a feature used to describe or predict market behavior; research needs to track when that information becomes available. Decision-making and automated research FinRL studies sequential decision-making; RD-Agent-Quant lets agents iterate on factors and models. Evaluation considers returns, risk, turnover, transaction costs, and performance across different market periods. 2020 Qlib A complete quantitative research workflow 2021–2023 FinRL / FinGPT Decisions and financial language models 2025 RD-Agent-Quant Joint factor and model optimization 01 2020 · Qlib · Quantitative workflow Qlib: An AI-oriented Quantitative Investment Platform How do data, models, portfolios, and backtesting form a research workflow? Read paper summary ↗ 2020 · arXiv × Qlib: An AI-oriented Quantitative Investment Platform Original paper ↗ Project and code ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Figure 1 · Original paper Research question How do data, models, portfolios, and backtesting form a research workflow? Core method Connect financial data processing and machine learning pipelines to strategy evaluation so that different models can be compared within a common workflow. Why this paper It places the model within a workflow from data preparation to strategy evaluation. What to focus on Trace the data flow through the framework diagram, then identify the time split, labels, and backtesting configuration in an example. Limitations and open questions Backtests depend on time splits, information availability, trading costs, and strategy selection. Historical backtest performance does not guarantee future returns. Look-ahead bias Using information in a prediction or decision that would not yet have been available at that time. Graph learning and time series: studying relationships and change Traffic, social interactions, transactions, and power grids all contain relationships and change over time. Graph learning models relationships and information on nodes, edges, or entire graphs; time-series modeling studies patterns over time and forecasts future values. The two can also be combined for spatiotemporal prediction. Watch the process ↗ Nodes, edges, and overall structure Graph tasks can predict node classes, whether a relationship exists, or properties of an entire graph. Molecular graphs and social networks share methods such as message passing, but their labels and evaluation differ. Trends, cycles, and forecasting Time-series research distinguishes trends, cycles, and anomalies, and compares statistical methods with deep learning. Testing moves forward in time to match how forecasting is used in practice. Spatiotemporal systems Traffic conditions change over time across a connected road network. Models need to capture spatial dependencies while accounting for external events and different time scales. Relationships Graphs and message passing Node, edge, and whole-graph tasks Change Trends and cycles Forecasting in temporal order Combination Spatiotemporal graphs Dynamic systems such as traffic Papers and learning resources Stanford CS224W ↗ Graph machine learning course Forecasting: Principles and Practice ↗ Statistical forecasting textbook · R tsai ↗ Python time-series tools Message passing Nodes aggregate information from neighbors and edges, updating their representations layer by layer. Rolling forecasting Repeatedly predicting a subsequent interval using only the data available as time moves forward. AutoML: selecting models and training configurations automatically Learning rate, tree depth, feature processing, and network architecture all affect results. AutoML studies how to automatically find better models and training configurations for a given task and computational budget. Watch the process ↗ Hyperparameter optimization Methods such as grid search, random search, and Bayesian optimization choose the next configuration. Optuna supports dynamic search spaces and pruning, stopping poorly performing trials early. Model and pipeline selection Automatically select data preprocessing, feature processing, models, and ensembles. For comparisons, keep data splits and budgets fixed and record the search cost. Use validation data to select configurations and reserve the test set for final evaluation. Architecture search and meta-learning Neural architecture search (NAS) looks for network structures; meta-learning uses experience from past tasks to help with new ones. Research can explore how to reduce search costs and transfer across tasks. Configuration HPO Hyperparameters such as learning rate Pipeline Model and feature selection The complete learning pipeline Architecture and experience NAS / Meta-learning Architecture search and knowledge across tasks 01 2019 · Optuna · Hyperparameter search Optuna: A Next-generation Hyperparameter Optimization Framework How can a search find a good training configuration within a limited budget? Read paper summary ↗ 2019 · KDD × Optuna: A Next-generation Hyperparameter Optimization Framework Original paper ↗ Project and code ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Akiba et al. · Figure 6 · Original paper Research question How can a search find a good training configuration within a limited budget? Core method Define the search space in code, then combine sampling and pruning to allocate the budget across trials. Why this paper It treats tuning as selecting trials within a budget and recording their results. What to focus on Start with the search space and trial loop, then examine how early stopping saves computation. Limitations and open questions Search depends on the budget, search space, and validation signal. Repeated selection can overfit validation data; keep an independent test set for final evaluation. Papers and learning resources AutoML textbook ↗ Methods, systems, and open questions Optuna ↗ Search, pruning, and visualization Optuna paper ↗ 2019 · KDD Hyperparameter A setting chosen before training, such as learning rate, regularization strength, or number of layers. Pruning Using intermediate results to stop less promising training runs and save the budget for other trials. Automated research: turning ideas into experiments and learning from the results Many steps in research can be carried out by software: searching for information, proposing candidates, changing code, running experiments, analyzing results, and writing reports. Automated research systems try to connect these steps so that each result informs the next experiment. Watch the process ↗ The experimental loop autoresearch focuses on language model training experiments on a single GPU, letting an agent modify training code and compare results. Evaluation metrics determine whether changes are kept, and experiments have a fixed training budget. From ideas to papers AI Scientist brings experimental design, code execution, result analysis, and paper writing into one workflow. Version 2 also explores agentic tree search. Research evidence and records Each candidate is linked to its configuration, code version, run logs, and results. When reading about these systems, trace a conclusion back to the experiments that support it, and examine how failed candidates affect later choices. 2024 AI Scientist Experiments, analysis, and writing 2025 AI Scientist-v2 Agentic tree search Training experiments autoresearch Iteration within a fixed budget 01 2025 · AI Scientist-v2 · Automated research The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search How can experimental results guide the next round of research? Core method Use agentic tree search to organize experiments, connecting plans, execution, analysis, and paper writing. Why this paper It makes each stage of an automated research process available for separate inspection. What to focus on Start with one complete experimental branch and check whether the final claims correspond to actual results. Limitations and open questions The study covers limited ML settings and reports that one of three autonomous workshop submissions met acceptance standards. This does not establish reliable autonomous discovery across disciplines. Papers and learning resources AI Scientist ↗ Original system and experiment templates AI Scientist-v2 ↗ 2025 · A research workflow using tree search autoresearch ↗ Automatically iterating on training experiments Experiment budget The resources allocated to an experiment, such as training time, computing power, or number of calls. Agentic tree search Organizing experimental plans and subsequent changes as a tree, then using existing results to guide further exploration. RSI: Can a system improve its own ability to improve? Recursive self-improvement (RSI) asks a further question: after a system modifies itself, can it become better at making the next improvement? Research can target an agent's code, tools, or search strategy, and can also involve learning algorithms. Watch the process ↗ What is being modified? AutoML usually searches configurations within a predefined space; automated research systems work on external research questions; self-improving systems also modify how they themselves work. When reading, first identify the code, strategies, or parameters that actually change. Storing and selecting versions Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM) lets a coding agent modify its own code, saves multiple versions, and uses coding tasks to evaluate them before exploring further. Its central loop creates, tests, retains, and modifies versions again. Observing sustained improvement Alongside scores on individual tasks, compare improvement curves over multiple rounds, total computation cost, and performance on new tasks. Use controls to distinguish improvements in the next round that come from changes in system capability from those that come from spending more on search. Propose changes Own code and tools Create a new version Run tests Fixed tasks and budget Compare changes in capability Continue improving Version archive and selection Track effects over multiple rounds 01 2025 · DGM · Self-improvement Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents Can a coding agent improve its abilities by modifying its own code? Read paper summary ↗ 2025 · arXiv × Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents Original paper ↗ Figure excerpt from the paper · Figure 1 · Original paper Research question Can a coding agent improve its abilities by modifying its own code? Core method Maintain multiple agent versions, generate self-modifications, and select candidates using coding tasks, creating an expanding version tree. Why this paper It separates improvements to agent code from parameter training and evaluation-based selection. What to focus on Start with one specific code change, then examine version selection, evaluation tasks, and the computation budget. Limitations and open questions Changes are selected on specific coding benchmarks and modify agent code, not the foundation model weights. This does not prove that arbitrary self-modification is beneficial. Papers and learning resources Darwin Gödel Machine ↗ 2025 · A coding agent that improves itself DGM project introduction ↗ Methods, experiments, and code AlphaEvolve ↗ Comparison: code search with an evaluator Self-modification A system changes its own code, tools, or strategies. DGM mainly modifies agent code. Recursive improvement An improvement that also changes the system's ability to make further improvements in later iterations. Match the evidence to the scientific claim Before comparing models, identify the sample: a molecular structure, a patient, a donor, a trial, or a market at a particular time. Related samples can share information. New molecular scaffolds, protein families, donors, centers, and future periods therefore represent different generalization questions. Area A distinction to check when reading a paper Molecules and proteins A predicted structure, favorable score, or computed energy differs from measured activity, successful synthesis, or stability under the intended conditions. Physical modeling Small training residuals do not guarantee an exact solution. Inspect boundary conditions, units, discretization, and errors over the required time horizon. Cells and genomics Expression prediction or an association network does not alone establish a regulatory mechanism. Examine the controls, perturbations, and biological context. EEG and imaging Match evaluation to participants or patients, sessions, and acquisition sites. A plausible reconstructed image or accurate contour supports a narrower claim than clinical usefulness or unrestricted neural decoding. Finance Preserve temporal information availability and account for transaction costs and repeated strategy selection. A historical backtest is evidence about that historical protocol, not a guaranteed future outcome. Mathematics A proof checker verifies the formal statement under its definitions and assumptions. For program search, establish what the evaluator tests and whether it proves correctness or only checks examples. Automated research and self-improvement Separate proposing, selecting, and independently verifying a change. Repeated gains on a reused evaluator can reflect search and selection; inspect held-out tasks and total search cost. The Qlib workflow documentation makes chronological splits and backtesting costs concrete; Mathematics in Lean explains formal statements and proofs. These examples show how definitions within a domain determine what counts as evidence. For each paper, write a short reading note: question → measured data → representation and assumptions → reference method → validation → supported conclusion . Include units, sources of measurement error, and the population or conditions to which the result applies. Consult a knowledgeable domain collaborator when those definitions are unfamiliar. Writing such a note is useful preparation for a new interdisciplinary project. AI for Science resource index · AI4X resource directory · Research questions · Contact and collaboration Research design covers comparisons and uncertainty; data and evaluation covers split design. For deeper prerequisites, use graphs , time series , causal inference , and probabilistic modeling . Responsible AI discusses affected populations and use settings.

title: Choose one domain and one kind of question
body: You do not need to learn every field below. Start with one familiar domain and learn its units, measurement processes, and established methods alongside machine-learning foundations . Follow a single paper from its scientific question to its input representation, prediction target, and validation. Use the animations to understand the workflow; they illustrate concepts rather than reproduce a paper's results. Distinguish prediction of a measured outcome, design of a candidate, simulation of a system, and decision-making about the next action or measurement. A stronger predictor may help one of these steps without validating the full scientific workflow. The sections below offer suggested reading, not an exhaustive history or a ranking of models.

title: Chemistry and materials: predicting properties, planning reactions, and discovering materials
body: Will a molecule dissolve readily in water? Is a crystal stable? What will a set of reactants produce? AI can predict properties and screen candidates from structures and experimental records. It can also learn energies and forces to reduce the computational cost of molecular dynamics. Watch the process ↗

title: Property prediction
body: Represent a molecule as a graph of atoms and bonds, or as a structure with three-dimensional coordinates, to predict quantities such as solubility and energy. The MPNN paper is a classic introduction to graph learning for quantum chemistry.

title: Reactions and synthesis
body: Forward prediction infers products from reactants; retrosynthesis works backward from a target molecule to find precursors and synthesis routes. Molecular Transformer models the SMILES strings of reactants and products as sequences.

title: Materials discovery and simulation
body: GNoME combines graph networks with first-principles calculations to screen for stable crystals. Deep Potential learns potential energy to provide the energies and forces needed for molecular dynamics. Active learning uses existing results to select the next calculations or experiments. 2017 MPNN Structure → properties 2018–2019 Deep Potential / Molecular Transformer Simulation and reaction prediction 2023 GNoME Model screening + DFT validation 01 2017 · MPNN · Molecular graphs Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry How can atoms and their relationships predict molecular properties? title: Physics and weather: learning solutions and predicting how systems evolve
body: Fluid flow, heat transfer, and weather forecasting involve physical quantities that vary across space and time. AI can approximate solutions to the equations that describe these processes, or use observations to predict how physical systems evolve. Watch the process ↗

title: Bringing equations into training
body: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) incorporate equation residuals, boundary conditions, and observation errors into training. Research examines how these constraints help, and how models handle complex domains and changes across multiple scales.

title: Learning solutions for a family of problems
body: Neural operators learn mappings from functions to functions, such as predicting an entire flow field from initial conditions. FNO constructs operations in the frequency domain, trains on solutions to a set of problems, and then handles new input conditions.

title: Forecasting weather and uncertainty
body: GraphCast uses graph networks to predict global weather fields. Later probabilistic forecasting approaches describe uncertainty through multiple possible futures. Researchers compare forecast errors, performance on extreme weather, and computation time. 2019 PINNs Equation constraints in training 2021 FNO Learning mappings between functions 2023 GraphCast Predicting global weather fields 01 2021 · FNO · Neural operators Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations How can a model learn the map from input functions, such as initial conditions or coefficients, to equation solutions? title: Proteins and enzymes: from sequence and structure to functional design
body: Proteins consist of amino acid sequences, and their folded structures are closely linked to what they can do. AI can predict structures, find natural sequences with desired properties, or propose new designs. Watch the process ↗

title: Representation and structure prediction
body: Protein language models learn transferable features from sequences. AlphaFold2 combines sequences, evolutionary information, and geometric relationships to predict three-dimensional structures. AlphaFold3 extends this to complexes containing proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules, and other components.

title: Sequence and backbone design
body: ProteinMPNN designs sequences for a given backbone; RFdiffusion generates backbones that satisfy constraints; ESM3 jointly uses sequence, structure, and function information. The design workflow then checks expression, stability, binding, or catalytic activity.

title: Enzyme mining and engineering
body: Enzyme mining finds candidates in natural sequence libraries; enzyme engineering modifies existing enzymes; de novo design builds new candidates around a target reaction. VenusMine retrieves candidates using structural and sequence clues, while VenusRXN matches enzymes starting from chemical reactions. 2021 AlphaFold2 Structure prediction 2022–2023 ProteinMPNN / RFdiffusion Sequence and backbone design 2025–2026 AMix-1 / AMix-2 Conditional generation and protein–text modeling Read further

title: The experimental loop in enzyme engineering
body: Zero-shot scoring can first rank mutations. A small amount of measured data can be used to fit a model of a specific property, while active learning uses existing results and uncertainty to choose the next experiments. Each round adds newly measured activity or stability to the data and updates the candidate ranking.

title: Constraints in de novo design
body: One approach finds a backbone to support a catalytic core; another organizes local interactions within an existing backbone. Catalytic geometry, foldability, stability, and reaction conditions all determine which experiments are needed next.

title: New approaches to foundation models
body: AMix-1 models proteins with Bayesian flow networks and explores conditioning on multiple sequence alignments and inference-time search. AMix-2 unifies protein and text modeling, using causal generation between blocks and diffusion within each block. When reading, trace the roles of conditioning inputs, candidate generation, and verifiers separately. 01 2021 · AlphaFold2 · Protein structure Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold How can sequence information support three-dimensional structure prediction? title: Genomics: how sequence changes affect gene regulation
body: DNA variants can alter protein coding, but they can also affect regulatory elements, expression, or splicing. Genomic models learn relationships within long sequences to predict these signals, helping researchers investigate the possible effects of a variant. Watch the process ↗

title: From sequence to signals
body: Models take a DNA sequence as input and predict experimental signals, such as expression, chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding, or splicing.

title: Comparing sequences before and after a variant
body: Input the original and variant sequences separately and compare their predictions. AlphaGenome is a representative model combining long sequences with multiple prediction tasks.

title: Connecting to cellular context
body: The same variant can have different effects in different tissues or cell states. Connecting sequence models with cell models requires aligning tissues, conditions, and what is measured. title: Cells: understanding states and predicting responses to interventions
body: Single-cell RNA sequencing measures noisy samples of gene expression from individual cells. Researchers study not only a cell's type and state, but also how it will respond to a genetic change or a drug. Spatial omics also preserves the locations of cells within tissue. Watch the process ↗

title: Cell representations
body: Geneformer, scGPT, and UCE learn gene or cell representations from large amounts of single-cell data for tasks such as annotation and integration. Data processing needs to preserve biological differences while handling sequencing depth, noise, and batch effects.

title: Perturbations and virtual cells
body: Given a cellular context and a genetic or drug perturbation, predict changes in expression. Virtual cells aim to connect modalities, scales, and dynamic processes more broadly; perturbation response is one clearly defined research task within this goal.

title: Spatial relationships and biomanufacturing
body: FLAG predicts spatial gene expression from pathology images, focusing on relationships between genes and between tissue locations. Biomanufacturing also studies metabolic networks, expression burden, and resource allocation to help propose strain modifications. title: States, dynamics, and dataset construction
body: Many single-cell datasets are snapshots measured from different cells. Studying changes over time requires sampling times, lineage information, or perturbation experiments. Data should record tissue, donor, batch, and measurement modality; perturbation data should also record the target, dose, time, and control.

title: EEG: from neural signals to state recognition and decoding
body: Electroencephalography (EEG) records how electrical signals at scalp electrodes change over time. AI can help recognize states, detect events, learn representations across participants, and connect signals with stimuli such as images that participants see. Watch the process ↗

title: Temporal and spatial representations
body: Electrode locations, sampling rate, filtering, and artifact handling together define the input. Models use frequency bands, changes over time, and relationships between channels.

title: Foundation models and transfer
body: After pretraining, the encoder can be frozen for linear probing or fine-tuned. Testing within the same participant and on new participants answers different questions. EEG-FM-Compass organizes these types of evaluation.

title: Visual decoding and generation
body: DreamDiffusion connects EEG representations to a pretrained image generation model and uses CLIP visual supervision. EEG-CLIP offers another alignment approach; compare how the two connect signals with images. title: Mathematics and algorithms: finding proofs and better constructions
body: AI in mathematics can propose proof steps, add geometric constructions, or search for objects that satisfy constraints and for more efficient algorithms. A key advantage is that many candidates can be checked using formal proof systems, programs, or exact computation. Watch the process ↗

title: Proof search
body: AlphaGeometry combines auxiliary constructions proposed by a language model with symbolic reasoning. Formal proof approaches express propositions and steps in systems such as Lean, where a kernel checks the proof.

title: Mathematical constructions
body: FunSearch lets a language model propose programs, then runs an evaluation function to select useful candidates. The paper studies combinatorial problems including cap sets. The model searches for programs that produce constructions.

title: Algorithm discovery
body: AlphaEvolve combines code generation, evaluators, and evolutionary search to find better algorithms and mathematical constructions. Runtime, correctness, or objective values can provide feedback. 2023 FunSearch Program generation + evaluation 2024 AlphaGeometry / AlphaProof Construction search and proofs 2025 AlphaEvolve Iterative algorithm optimization 01 2024 · AlphaGeometry · Geometry proofs Solving olympiad geometry without human demonstrations How can auxiliary constructions and symbolic reasoning work together to find a proof? title: Finance: from text and time-series data to predictions and decisions
body: Financial AI includes understanding financial reports and news, identifying risks, forecasting time series, constructing portfolios, and executing trades. Model inputs include structured data such as prices and trading volume, as well as text from announcements and reports. Watch the process ↗

title: Financial text
body: FinGPT offers an entry point to financial language models, data, and fine-tuning. Tasks such as sentiment analysis, event extraction, and information extraction illustrate how language models can be used in this domain.

title: Quantitative prediction and backtesting
body: Qlib connects data processing, features, models, portfolios, and backtesting. A factor is a feature used to describe or predict market behavior; research needs to track when that information becomes available.

title: Graph learning and time series: studying relationships and change
body: Traffic, social interactions, transactions, and power grids all contain relationships and change over time. Graph learning models relationships and information on nodes, edges, or entire graphs; time-series modeling studies patterns over time and forecasts future values. The two can also be combined for spatiotemporal prediction. Watch the process ↗

title: Nodes, edges, and overall structure
body: Graph tasks can predict node classes, whether a relationship exists, or properties of an entire graph. Molecular graphs and social networks share methods such as message passing, but their labels and evaluation differ.

title: Trends, cycles, and forecasting
body: Time-series research distinguishes trends, cycles, and anomalies, and compares statistical methods with deep learning. Testing moves forward in time to match how forecasting is used in practice.

body: Traffic conditions change over time across a connected road network. Models need to capture spatial dependencies while accounting for external events and different time scales. title: AutoML: selecting models and training configurations automatically
body: Learning rate, tree depth, feature processing, and network architecture all affect results. AutoML studies how to automatically find better models and training configurations for a given task and computational budget. Watch the process ↗

title: Automated research: turning ideas into experiments and learning from the results
body: Many steps in research can be carried out by software: searching for information, proposing candidates, changing code, running experiments, analyzing results, and writing reports. title: RSI: Can a system improve its own ability to improve?
body: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) asks a further question: after a system modifies itself, can it become better at making the next improvement? Research can target an agent's code, tools, or search strategy, and can also involve learning algorithms. Watch the process ↗

title: What is being modified?
body: AutoML usually searches configurations within a predefined space; automated research systems work on external research questions; self-improving systems also modify how they themselves work. When reading, first identify the code, strategies, or parameters that actually change.

title: Storing and selecting versions
body: Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM) lets a coding agent modify its own code, saves multiple versions, and uses coding tasks to evaluate them before exploring further. Its central loop creates, tests, retains, and modifies versions again.

title: Observing sustained improvement
body: Alongside scores on individual tasks, compare improvement curves over multiple rounds, total computation cost, and performance on new tasks. Use controls to distinguish improvements in the next round that come from changes in system capability from those that come from spending more on search.
